rationale: Tentative qualitative of ⲗⲟ 'stop, abide, remain' — designating the indweller (Mind/soul) within the body. The diacritic ⲗⲏⲟ́ is preserved in transcription. Alternative readings include 'him who is at rest' or 'him who has ceased.' Context: chapter title about the body's 'gate of bringing-forth' for him who is within.
Probable compound containing ⲣ̄-ⲡⲱϣ 'help, share.' Parallels phylakes (Greek 'guards') in the inventory of beings stationed at the body's gates. Tentative.
In context of guards over gates and the Mind taking control, 'keys' fits as the means of opening/shutting. Crum has ϣⲁϣⲧ in this semantic field. Alternative: 'instruments of force, control.'
Greek τρυφή 'sensual delight, luxurious living.' Fits the negative-cosmological catalogue of vices contrasted with righteousness. Coptic Lyc. orthography τ→ⲧ, υ→ⲁ.

Compound: ⲣⲟ 'gate/mouth' + genitive + ϩⲉⲓⲛⲉ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'bringing forth' (verbal noun of ⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'bring' + directional ⲁⲃⲁⲗ). Designates the body's orifices/sense-organs as gates that bring forth the inner life. Title of Kephalaion 142.
Possibly 'those that send out' (ⲧⲛ̄ⲛⲁⲩ = 'send' or 'see-out'). Listed as a sense-faculty of the body alongside seeing, hearing, smelling, and speaking.
